bull.b: Successful piloted transitions and repeatable public demonstrations provide tangible evidence that the VX4/Valo program is advancing beyond design work. Two aircraft also increase testing capacity, supporting faster technical learning and gradual de-risking of the path toward certification.

Planned assembly and battery-capacity investments establish a clearer bridge from prototype development to production readiness. Increasing internal battery capability and preparing pilot manufacturing can support program control, future scale, and the company’s broader electric and hybrid aircraft strategy.

The breadth of technology, infrastructure, airspace-integration, customer, and regulatory relationships strengthens the platform’s development ecosystem. These collaborations can improve technical validation and international market access, while supporting applications across passenger, autonomous, hybrid, and defence markets.

bear.b: Minimal revenue and continuing operating losses show that the business has not yet achieved commercial scale or self-sustaining economics. Until certification and customer commitments translate into deliveries, the company remains exposed to extended development periods and uncertain timing for meaningful revenue growth.

Persistent negative cash generation means operations and development must continue to be financed externally rather than funded by the business. A large ongoing burn rate can constrain investment flexibility and increase the importance of successful financing, certification progress, and disciplined execution.

Moving the certification target to 2029 extends the period before commercial aircraft deliveries and revenue can scale. Combined with substantial projected cash outflows, the delay increases reliance on future financing and government support and leaves more time for execution or regulatory setbacks.
